chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Rifah al-Nakhas said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: 'I bargained with a man for a female slave, and he sold her to me for my valuation (hukmi). I took possession of her from him on that basis. Then I sent him one thousand dirhams, saying:

He said: 'I see that you should value the female slave with a fair valuation. If her value is more than what you sent him, it is upon you to return to him the deficiency of the value. And if her value is less than what you sent him, it is his.' I said: 'What do you think if I found a defect in her after I had taken possession of her?' He said: 'You do not have the right to return her, but you have the right to take the value of the difference between her soundness and the defect.'

key_terms.بِحُكْمِي: by my valuation (a type of sale where price is determined by one party's assessment)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a defect is found in a purchased slave after possession in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanics of *al-Hukm* (arbitrated valuation) in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that possession (*qabd*) validates the transfer of risk and ownership even before final settlement. It further distinguishes between the right of return (*khiyar al-'ayb*) and the right to claim value difference, ruling that post-possession defects do not void the contract but entitle the buyer to compensation for the diminution in value.
